candidates.name: sideye/airbnb-occupancy-tax
candidates.what_it_holds: Economics honors thesis studying Boston's Airbnb occupancy-tax implementation (2018-2019). Committed Jupyter notebooks (e.g. 'Calculate Exits.ipynb') and CSVs with listing-level reservation-date metrics (weekly/bimonthly/monthly aggregations), 'date booked' monthly aggregation, and an entries/exits analysis. Treatment city Boston plus control cities Montreal, Providence/Rhode Island, Washington DC, Quebec City, Nashville, San Francisco, Chicago, Twin Cities, Denver, Asheville, with a control-city tax-rate spreadsheet. Filters to listings booked >14 nights/year (the tax threshold) and applies synthetic-control methodology around each city's tax-implementation date.
candidates.why_useful: Directly on-theme: a natural-experiment dataset on how STR occupancy-tax implementation affects Airbnb listing/booking behavior across 11 North American cities, with before/after listing-level data. Could inform how new occupancy-tax regimes (gap #12 regulation trackers, also relevant to nights/ADR elasticity work) affect nights and host supply; a template for a similar study on newer tax rollouts.
candidates.size_hint: several CSVs + notebooks, listing-level aggregated data, not large

candidates.name: csabasidor/occupancy_tax_payers_identifier
candidates.what_it_holds: Python + PostgreSQL scripts (01_fb_place_search_downloader.py, 02_google_places_api_downloader.py, plus more in the sequence) that harvest candidate short-term-lodging providers within an administrative boundary via Facebook Place Search API, Google Places API and Foursquare Places API, intended to identify who owes local occupancy tax.
candidates.why_useful: A working method (not sanctioned for us to run, per repo rules on non-Airbnb scraping decisions) for cross-checking STR supply density against tax-registration compliance in a given city; template for a compliance/coverage cross-check on municipal STR registries we already hold.
candidates.size_hint: code only, no committed data output

candidates.name: devillers/taxes-de-sejour
candidates.what_it_holds: Next.js/MongoDB web app for French conciergeries/hosts/communes to compute and remit taxe de sejour from uploaded stay-record CSVs. Repo ships data/owners.csv (70KB), data/properties.csv (82KB) and data/taxes.csv (10KB), but these read as sample/seed fixtures for the app (owner names, property addresses) rather than real municipal tax-collection totals.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal: the underlying rate-calculation logic reflects real French taxe de sejour rules, but the committed CSVs appear to be synthetic demo data, not actual remittance figures for any commune.
candidates.geography: France (generic, no specific commune data confirmed)

candidates.name: arcam-vd/e-arcam
candidates.what_it_holds: Cyberadministration webapp for a Swiss regional association (Cossonay-Aubonne-Morges, Vaud canton) to administer taxe de sejour collection. Appears to be the admin tool itself, not a public dataset of collections figures.
candidates.why_useful: Low relevance: shows the administrative software side of tourist-tax collection in a small Swiss region, no ABNB-scale data.

candidates.name: fracabu/tassa_soggiorno_app
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed Streamlit app that calculates Rome's imposta di soggiorno (tourist occupancy tax) based on booking details per local regulations. Calculation logic only; no committed historical collections data found.
candidates.why_useful: Encodes current Rome tourist-tax rate rules/brackets in code, which could be reused to compute implied tax revenue from Rome nights/ADR estimates, but holds no dataset itself.

candidates.name: Kenneth-Rakentine/30_Night_Occupancy_Tax_Calculator
candidates.what_it_holds: Tool that parses uploaded hotel/STR folios to determine 30-night reimbursement eligibility and calculate occupancy-tax reimbursement totals (US, likely North Carolina style long-stay exemption).
candidates.why_useful: Marginal utility: a folio-parsing calculator, not a public dataset; only useful as a template if we ever process our own folio-style data.

candidates.name: AyhamAlghoul/2025-Bexar-County-Proposition-B-Results-by-Precinct
candidates.what_it_holds: Interactive precinct-level election-results map for a 2025 Bexar County (San Antonio, TX) referendum on a hotel occupancy tax increase to fund stadium construction, with precinct vote data.
candidates.why_useful: Only tangentially related: shows local political appetite for raising hotel/occupancy taxes in one US county, not a national or ABNB-relevant collections series. Flagging for completeness only.

notes: This theme is thin on GitHub: official tourist-tax collection statistics (Paris taxe de sejour receipts, Amsterdam toeristenbelasting revenue, Italian comune-level imposta di soggiorno totals, or any Airbnb-published occupancy-tax remittance report) do not appear to be mirrored as committed datasets in any repo found across 6 gh search queries (taxe de sejour / imposta di soggiorno / imposta soggiorno / toeristenbelasting / tourist tax dataset / occupancy tax). What exists instead is: (1) small calculator/admin webapps that encode current tax rates and calculation logic (France, Rome, Switzerland, generic US) but ship no real historical collections data, mostly with synthetic/seed CSVs; (2) one genuinely useful item, sideye/airbnb-occupancy-tax, a 2018-2019 Boston-vs-control-cities natural-experiment dataset on occupancy-tax rollout and Airbnb listing behavior; (3) one non-Airbnb STR-compliance identification scraper method (csabasidor). Two repos returned empty/dead (btourman/taxe-de-sejour: only .gitignore + blank README) and were excluded per the cataloguing rules. WebSearch was unavailable for this scout (session budget of 200 exhausted by other concurrent scouts before I could use it), which limited fallback discovery once gh search calls hit the 6-call cap; WebFetch on etalab's GitHub org and data.gouv.fr's tourist-tax search also came back empty (data.gouv.fr almost certainly hosts an official taxe de sejour dataset from DGFiP, but its GitHub-mirror status, if any, could not be confirmed without a working search). Recommend a future scout with WebSearch quota try: 'data.gouv.fr taxe de sejour DGFiP github', 'Airbnb tax collection agreements list scraper github', 'CBS Amsterdam toeristenbelasting opendata github', and Italian comune open-data portals (dati.comune.roma.it, dati.venezia.it) for imposta di soggiorno mirrors — none of these were reachable with the tools available this run.
